source.title: Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930, p. 7 ("Local elections in Ulster: no contests for seats on Antrim County Council; list of nominations"); Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1933, p. 9 ("Ulster elections: nominations for Antrim County Council (23 ordinary members)")
source.publisher: Belfast News-Letter (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: twenty-three divisions, not nineteen: the News-Letter's list of 8 May 1930 prints 19 nominations, but the county had 23 ordinary members (Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1933, p. 9: 'There are 23 ordinary members'; Irish News, 4 May 1933, p. 3 lists all 23 divisions), and the four divisions absent from the 1930 list are exactly those whose retiring members are recorded as sitting in 1933. The 1930 list is a list of nominations received; a division with no nomination is not in it.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received by Andrew (Alexander) Millar, secretary, at the County Courthouse, Belfast, on 7 May 1930, and there were no contests in any division (Belfast News-Letter, 8 May 1930). No poll was therefore held: the statutory election day was Thursday 5 June 1930, the day fixed for the local elections that year (Belfast municipal polling '5th June', Belfast News-Letter, 7 May 1930, p. 9; guardians election 'Thursday, 5th June', Irish News, 30 April 1930, p. 6). The queue's provisional 29 May is not supported by any source seen. The News-Letter prints no party labels and no sitting-member asterisks, so neither is given. Added from reports of the new council's meetings early in the term, each division inferred from the previous return: Dunminning, Kirkinriola and Glenarm. Returned unopposed.
